ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which child nodes are of the type and reports where they are, as runs of consecutive nodes of the type. Hops 1, 2 and 3 pass the child list along and create or wrap the result; hop 4 only adds the nodes of each run the gold reports, in order, and adds no node outside a reported run. When the gold leaves the run that ends at the end of the list unreported, its nodes can reach the result only if a caller re-tests the nodes itself (a second implementation of the gold's decision, contrary to hop 4's documented role) or replaces the gold. The gold's javadoc promises the runs of consecutive nodes of the type; the variant omits the run [0, 1) of the script element's child list. The convention (every child of the selected type is selected, the last child included) is pinned outside the gold by the intact sibling filters Element.textNodes and Element.children over the same child list, and by the passing tests ElementTest::testGetTextNodes (the last child ' Four' is selected), TextNodeTest::testWithSupplementaryCharacter (the body's only and last child is selected) and ElementTest::testManipulateTextNodes (the split-off last child is counted).
